name: Urothelial Carcinoma of the Bladder, TURBT, and Radical Cystectomy

reference.source: Sabiston Textbook of Surgery 22nd ed / Campbell-Walsh Urology 12th ed
clinicalPearls: Painless gross hematuria throughout the urinary stream represents bladder cancer until proven otherwise
Cigarette smoking is the leading risk factor; aromatic industrial amines (benzidine) also strongly predispose
Presence of detrusor muscularis propria in TURBT specimen is mandatory to determine muscle-invasive status
Non-muscle-invasive high-risk cancer receives transurethral resection followed by intravesical BCG immunotherapy
Muscle-invasive bladder cancer (T2+) requires neoadjuvant cisplatin chemotherapy and radical cystectomy
reference.pathophysiology: Urothelial carcinoma develops along dual molecular pathways: low-grade papillary tumors driven by FGFR3 and PIK3CA activating mutations with low invasive potential, and high-grade invasive carcinomas driven by TP53 and RB1 tumor suppressor loss with high propensity for detrusor invasion, lymph node spread, and distant visceral metastasis.
additionalDifferentials: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with friable mucosal bleeding
Schistosoma haematobium bilharzial cystitis / squamous cell carcinoma
additionalInvestigations: Transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT) with muscularis propria sampling
CT urography of the abdomen and pelvis to evaluate upper tracts and perivesical fat
Chest computed tomography for systemic metastatic staging
